scenes.title: dbt Models & Materializations
scenes.narration: Here we look at dbt models and the materialization strategies that decide how each model is physically built in the warehouse.

scenes.title: What a model is
bullets: A model is a single SQL SELECT in a .sql file
The file name becomes the object name
dbt wraps it in the right create statement
scenes.narration: A dbt model is simply one SQL file containing a single SELECT statement. The name of the file becomes the name of the table or view dbt creates. Because you only write the SELECT, dbt is free to wrap it in whatever create-or-replace boilerplate the chosen materialization requires.

scenes.title: View versus Table

right.heading: table
points: Good for heavy or shared logic

scenes.narration: The two most common materializations are view and table. A view stores no data and recomputes its logic every time it is queried, which makes it ideal for lightweight staging where freshness matters more than speed. A table persists the results so reads are fast, but it is fully rebuilt on each dbt run, making it a better fit for heavy transformations or logic many people query.

scenes.title: Configuring a materialization
scenes.code:
-- models/marts/dim_customers.sql
{{ config(materialized='table') }}

select
    customer_id,
    lower(email) as email,
    created_at
from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}
scenes.narration: This model sets its materialization inline with a config block at the top, overriding any folder default. The body is just an ordinary SELECT that reads from an upstream staging model. When you run dbt, it will issue a create-table-as statement around this query, so you never write the DDL yourself. That separation of what you want from how it is built is the heart of dbt.

scenes.title: The other two materializations
bullets: incremental appends only new rows for large tables
ephemeral inlines logic as a CTE, building nothing
scenes.narration: Beyond views and tables, dbt offers incremental models that process only new rows to keep very large tables cheap to update, and ephemeral models that are never built at all but instead injected as a common table expression into the models that reference them.

scenes.text: Default to views for staging and tables for marts, and reach for incremental only when a table grows too large to rebuild fully.
scenes.narration: As a practical default, use views for your staging layer and tables for your marts, and only reach for incremental models once a table has grown too large to rebuild in full comfortably.
